title: DRIVE: Fine-tuning via Data Contribution- and Diversity-aware Weighting with Prior Regularization
abstract: arXiv:2610.32501v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Single-stage fine-tuning is pervasive, yet catastrophic forgetting persists when the source pre-training data is inaccessible. Data weighting affords a natural lever to modulate sample influence. Yet existing weighting methods lack a principled mechanism to explicitly arbitrate knowledge retention against new-task adaptation, and provide no unified differentiable objective to accommodate auxiliary signals such as sample diversity and sample characteristics. This is because current schemes privilege one goal over the other, and no explicit gradient-compatible encoding exists for such signals. translated_title: DRIVE：通过数据贡献与多样性感知的加权及先验正则化进行微调
translated_abstract: 单阶段微调十分普遍，然而当源预训练数据不可访问时，灾难性遗忘依然存在。数据加权为调节样本影响提供了一种自然的手段。然而，现有的加权方法缺乏一种有原则的机制来显式地权衡知识保持与新任务适应之间的关系，并且没有提供一个统一的可微目标来容纳诸如样本多样性和样本特征等辅助信号。这是因为当前的方案往往偏重其中一个目标而忽视另一个，且不存在针对这些信号的显式梯度兼容编码。为解决这一问题，我们提出了DRIVE，一个有原则且高效的权重分配框架。它通过一个统一的可微目标推导出每个样本的权重，其中三个耦合的信号共同演化：Shapley可加性将贡献分解为抗遗忘和适应两个分量，这些分量由基于协方差的多样性项进行重塑，并通过先验正则化加以稳定。
tldr: DRIVE提出了一个面向单阶段微调的统一可微数据加权框架，通过Shapley贡献分解（抗遗忘与适应分量）、基于协方差的多样性项和先验正则化三个耦合信号的共同演化，在源预训练数据不可访问的情况下显式平衡知识保持与新任务适应。
en_tdlr: DRIVE is a principled and efficient differentiable data-weighting framework for single-stage fine-tuning that co-evolves three coupled signals—Shapley-based contribution decomposition into anti-forgetting and adaptation components, a covariance-based diversity term, and prior regularization—to explicitly balance knowledge retention against new-task adaptation when source pre-training data is inaccessible.
